"The highest-efficiency delivery network powered by people already in flight. Secure, fast, and remarkably localized." KwikSenda makes global shipping feel personal. Instead of relying on traditional courier infrastructure, KwikSenda leverages the movement of real people — travelers with spare luggage capacity — to deliver packages faster, cheaper, and more reliably than conventional shipping methods. Mission Statement: "To move what truly matters, it takes people. Connecting communities across borders through the power of human traveler movement." Core Value Proposition KwikSenda reimagines global delivery across four key pillars: Benefit Description 💰 Drastic Savings Skip high-tier courier costs. Connect with travelers and save up to 80% on international shipping compared to services like DHL or FedEx. ⚡ Superior Speed Avoid customs delays and long transit times. Items move with people, arriving at the destination in global record time . 🛡️ Total Security Every traveler undergoes strict, multi-step background checks and full package protection protocols before being approved. 🤝 Personal Care Your package is not just cargo — it is personally handled by someone who understands its value to you. How It Works KwikSenda simplifies cross-border delivery into four clear steps — one seamless experience for both senders and travelers. Step 1 — Post & Discover This step is about visibility. Senders and travelers publish their intent on the platform so the right match can be made. For Senders: Post a delivery request that includes the following details: A description of the item being transported Its weight and volume The name and details of the intended recipient For Travelers: Post your upcoming journey details so senders can find and request you: Origin city/country Destination city/country Intended travel date Step 2 — Select & Match Once both parties are visible on the platform, the matching process begins. For Senders: Browse the list of available verified travelers and select one that best matches your: Delivery route Travel dates Capacity and delivery needs For Travelers: Get matched with a sender and their package. Review the full request details — including item type, weight, and handling instructions — and confirm whether you accept the delivery. Step 3 — Pay & Hand Over Once a match is confirmed, the transaction and physical handover take place. For Senders: Pay the full delivery fee securely through the KwikSenda platform. Your payment is held in escrow and is not released to the traveler until successful delivery is confirmed. For Travelers: Receive the physical package from the sender at the agreed-upon handover point. Your payment remains in escrow and is released to you upon confirmed delivery . Step 4 — Deliver & Get Paid The final step closes the loop for both parties. For Senders: Your package is delivered directly to the recipient. You can track every step in real time and confirm receipt in the app once delivery is complete. For Travelers: Deliver the package to the recipient and receive your payment within three days once the sender confirms receipt in the app. For Senders KwikSenda is built for anyone who needs to send a package across borders — affordably, safely, and on time. Whether you are part of the diaspora sending gifts home, a small business shipping products, or an individual sending personal items, KwikSenda connects you directly with trusted travelers. How to Post a Package Create or log in to your KwikSenda account Navigate to "Post a Delivery Request" Enter the item details: description, weight, volume, and fragility level Add the recipient's name and delivery address Specify the origin and destination Set any special handling instructions (e.g., "Handle with extreme care" ) Browse matched travelers and select your preferred carrier Pay securely through the platform — your payment is escrow-protected Package Example Field Detail Package ID #82 Route LHR → KGL (London to Kigali) Weight 1.5 kg Category Electronics (Fragile) Handling Note "Handle with extreme care" Payment Status Escrow Secured What Senders Can Expect Upfront, transparent pricing before confirming any booking Real-time tracking of your package during the journey Escrow-protected payment — your money is only released on successful delivery Full refund if a traveler cancels or delivers an item in poor condition Direct communication with the traveler through the platform For Travelers KwikSenda gives travelers a way to turn their existing journeys into earning opportunities — while helping senders get packages to loved ones across the world. "It's safe, easy, and a fun way to make money while traveling the world. Every delivery is backed by our comprehensive protection protocols." How to Post a Trip Create or log in to your KwikSenda account Navigate to "Post a Trip" Enter your journey details: origin, destination, and departure date Indicate your available carrying capacity (in kg) Set your availability for package pickup and delivery Wait to be matched with a sender whose request aligns with your route Review the package details and confirm the delivery Receive the package at the handover point and carry it to the destination Deliver to the recipient and receive your payment within 3 days of confirmed receipt Traveler Requirements Must complete the KwikSenda identity verification process Must pass multi-step background checks Must comply with applicable customs and import/export regulations for all routes Must handle all accepted packages with care in accordance with listed handling instructions Earning Potential Travelers can earn meaningful supplemental income by utilizing their spare luggage capacity. Payment & Escrow System The KwikSenda escrow model is central to the platform's trust framework. Here is how it works end to end: Stage What Happens Sender pays Full delivery fee is paid by the sender to KwikSenda — funds enter escrow Package handover Sender physically hands the package to the traveler In transit Funds remain held in escrow — neither party can access them Delivery confirmed Recipient confirms receipt in the app; sender approves Payment released Funds are released to the traveler within 3 days of confirmed receipt Dispute / Cancellation Full refund issued to sender; new traveler search initiated by KwikSenda The escrow system means neither party bears financial risk — senders are protected from loss, and travelers are guaranteed payment upon completion. Project Overview What is NextGenEMR? NextGenEMR is a secure, web-based Electronic Medical Record system designed for health post operations across Rwanda. It supports the complete patient journey — from initial registration through clinical consultation, diagnostics, pharmacy, billing, insurance, and long-term programme follow-up. 10: Project Overview: TeleRad is Rwanda's centralised teleradiology platform — a secure, national infrastructure for storing, managing, and reporting on DICOM imaging studies. It connects health facilities across the country to a network of verified radiologists who can review and report on studies remotely, from anywhere. Before TeleRad, access to radiology expertise was constrained by geography. Patients in district hospitals often waited days — or transferred facilities — for imaging reports. TeleRad eliminates that bottleneck. A study uploaded from a facility in Musanze or Huye reaches a radiologist in seconds, with findings returned the same day. By centralising this workflow under NHIC, Rwanda now has a single, auditable record of national radiology activity — a foundation for health intelligence that did not previously exist. What TeleRad Does TeleRad organises the teleradiology workflow into a clear, role-based process. A facility uploads an imaging study. It appears on a national worklist. An admin forwards it to the right radiologist, who reviews and submits a report. The study is marked as complete. Every step is logged. The platform is built around two roles: Admins manage the full platform — users, facilities, studies, and reporting activity. They have visibility across all facilities and all studies on the network, and can forward studies to specific radiologists with clinical notes. Radiologists have a focused interface showing only their assigned studies. They open studies in the integrated viewer, write and save report drafts, and submit final reports — all from one screen. Access is restricted to verified staff only. There is no self-registration. Accounts are created by an administrator, ensuring full control over who can access patient imaging data. Value for NHIC A live view of national radiology activity The platform's Statistics page gives NHIC something that did not exist before: a real-time, consolidated view of radiology reporting activity across the entire country. Study volumes by facility, by modality, by reporting status — all in one place, updated continuously. This is not just operational data. It is the beginning of a national health intelligence layer. For the first time, NHIC and the Ministry of Health can answer questions like: which facilities are generating the most unread studies? Where are reporting delays concentrated? What modalities are in highest demand nationally? Accountability built in Every action on TeleRad is logged and immutable. Sign-ins, report submissions, user changes, study forwards — all recorded with a timestamp and the identity of the user who performed the action. Logs cannot be modified or deleted through the platform. This level of auditability is a prerequisite for a national health platform. It supports clinical governance, data protection obligations, and institutional accountability without requiring any additional process. A growing map of Rwanda's diagnostic network Each facility connected to TeleRad represents a formal digital integration with national health infrastructure. As more facilities come online, the platform becomes a live picture of Rwanda's imaging capacity — which facilities are active, what equipment they have, and how much they are using it. This is data NHIC has never had at this level of granularity or reliability. Radiologist access, wherever they are TeleRad removes the geographic constraint on radiology expertise. A radiologist in Kigali can report on a study uploaded from a rural district hospital within the same working day. Weasis Desktop Setup Login Required — Desktop Setup Weasis is a free, open-source DICOM viewer that connects to your Orthanc server via DICOMweb. Follow the steps below to configure it for use with TeleRad. Prerequisites Download and install Weasis for your operating system from the official Weasis website Your Orthanc server must be running and accessible on the network Step 1 — Copy your DICOMweb URL from the web application Open a study in the TeleRad web viewer Click the Viewer dropdown in the top-right of the viewer Select "Copy DICOMweb URL" to copy the base URL — you will need this when configuring Weasis Note: If the study format is not supported in the browser, you will see the "This DICOM format is not supported for browser viewing" message. Use the "View Supported Viewers" button from that screen to navigate to this setup guide. Step 2 — Open Preferences in Weasis Navigate to File > Preferences (or press Alt + P on Windows/Linux; ⌘ , on macOS). Step 3 — Select the DICOM Node List In the Preferences window, select DICOM from the left-hand panel, then click DICOM node list . Step 4 — Add a new WEB Node Under the WEB Node section, click Add new and fill in the following fields: Field Value Description NHIC Orthanc (or any name you choose) Service Type DICOMWeb Service URL http://[your-host]/dicom-web Replace [your-host] with the hostname or IP address of your Orthanc server. For a local deployment this is typically localhost or 127.0.0.1 . Step 5 — Configure Authentication (if required) If your Orthanc instance requires HTTP Basic Authentication: Enable the Authentication toggle in the node configuration Enter your Username and Password Step 6 — Save Click OK / Save to close the Preferences window. Step 7 — Import a Study Go to File > Import > DICOMWeb Select your newly created node from the dropdown Search for the study by patient name, study date, or Study Instance UID Select a result and wait for the retrieval to complete Step 8 — View the Study Once retrieval is complete, double-click the study to open it in the viewer. 11: Project Overview: IEDS is Rwanda's nationally owned platform for mosquito surveillance and insecticide resistance data management. It brings together field entomology, laboratory science, and public health decision-making into a single, integrated system — built in-house by Global Kwik Koders and designed to serve everyone from field data collectors in rural sentinel sites to Ministry of Health leadership making vector control decisions at the national level. Before IEDS, Rwanda's entomological surveillance data lived in an externally managed platform controlled by a third party, dependent on external funding, and out of MoH’s direct authority. That dependency created real risk: when the relationship ended, so did access to the system. IEDS was built to close that gap permanently — giving Rwanda full data sovereignty over one of its most critical public health datasets. What IEDS Does IEDS operates across three environments that work together as one platform. The web application is the command centre. National entomologists design data collection instruments, review incoming data, and build dashboards. District malaria officers track resistance trends and generate reports. Analysts run queries and visualise patterns across time, geography, and species. Everything is role-based — each user sees and does exactly what their function requires, nothing more. The mobile application is built for the field. Data collectors at sentinel sites — often working in areas with limited or no internet connectivity — use the app to capture mosquito collection records, GPS coordinates, images, and bioassay results. The app saves everything locally and syncs automatically when connectivity returns. No data is lost between the field and the database. The DHIS2 integration connects IEDS to Rwanda's national health information infrastructure. Aggregated surveillance indicators flow into DHIS2 automatically, and malaria case data flows back in — enabling entomological and epidemiological data to be read together for the first time in a structured, repeatable way. Value for MoH/ NHIC/RBC Full ownership of a national surveillance asset IEDS is the first entomological surveillance platform Rwanda has built and owns entirely. The data, the infrastructure, the codebase — all of it sits under NHIC's institutional authority. There is no external dependency, no third-party contract, no risk of access being revoked. This is not a minor operational detail. Mosquito surveillance data underpins malaria vector control decisions for the entire country. Owning that data infrastructure is a strategic public health asset. From field to dashboard in under 24 hours The platform is designed to close the gap between data collection and decision-making. A field team collecting mosquitoes at a sentinel site in the morning can have that data visible on a national dashboard the same day — automatically validated, geospatially tagged, and linked to meteorological context. The target is under 24 hours from collection to dashboard visibility. For insecticide resistance in particular — where a new resistance pattern can change the recommended vector control strategy for an entire district — that speed matters enormously. A single national record of vector surveillance IEDS creates, for the first time, a unified and continuously updated record of mosquito surveillance activity across Rwanda's sentinel sites. Species composition, abundance indices, resistance classifications, trap data, bioassay results — all captured in structured, queryable form, linked to geography and time. This is the data infrastructure that makes evidence-based vector control possible at scale. District malaria officers no longer need to wait for periodic reports; the data is available to them directly, filtered to their geography, as it arrives. Built-in data quality assurance Every record that enters IEDS passes through validation at the point of entry — required fields enforced, data types checked, structured dropdowns constraining free-text errors. Import tools apply the same rules to bulk uploads. Duplicate detection flags suspicious combinations of site, date, form, and trap ID before they enter the dataset. Monthly data quality reviews are structured into the platform's workflow, with automated alerts when submission rates from enrolled sites fall below threshold. The result is a dataset that decision-makers can actually trust. Connection to the national health system Because IEDS integrates directly with DHIS2, entomological data does not live in isolation. Resistance trends can be read alongside malaria case incidence. Surveillance indicators become part of the same national health intelligence picture that MoH leadership uses to allocate resources and plan interventions. This is what makes IEDS more than a data management tool — it is a link between field science and national health governance. 1. 14: Project Overview: HEC MIS is the official platform for processing foreign qualification equivalency applications in Rwanda. It takes what was a manual, paper-based workflow — applications moving between officers through physical files, emails, and informal handoffs — and replaces it with a structured, fully digital process that is faster, consistent, and accountable at every step. When a Rwandan returning from studying abroad, or a foreign professional seeking to work in Rwanda, needs their qualification formally recognised, HEC MIS is where that process lives. From the moment an application is submitted through Irembo — Rwanda's national services portal — to the moment the Director General signs the equivalency certificate, every step happens in one system. What HEC MIS Does Every application follows a defined multi-level review pipeline. The system enforces the sequence — officers can only act on applications at their assigned level, and no application can skip a stage. An applicant submits their foreign qualification documents through Irembo and pays the processing fee. The application enters HEC MIS automatically, already confirmed as paid. From there, it moves through four levels of review: an initial officer checks the submitted documents and, where necessary, contacts the issuing university directly to verify authenticity. A second officer reviews the cleared application. A department head provides pre-approval sign-off. The Director General counter-signs and then applies the official digital signature — at which point the equivalency certificate is generated automatically and issued. At every level, officers can approve and move the application forward, reject it with a documented reason, or send it back for more information. Every decision is recorded, timestamped, and tied to the officer who made it. Applicants can track their application status in real time through Irembo, without needing to contact HEC directly. Value for HEC A process that can be trusted Before HEC MIS, the equivalency process depended heavily on individual diligence — applications could stall between review levels, documents could be lost, and there was no reliable way to know where any given application was in the pipeline. HEC MIS makes the process structural rather than personal. The system enforces every handoff, blocks steps from being skipped, and records every action. For an institution responsible for maintaining the integrity of Rwanda's higher education credentials, that structural reliability is foundational. University verification built into the workflow One of the most critical — and previously most fragile — steps in equivalency processing is verifying that academic documents are genuine. HEC MIS integrates this directly into the workflow. L1 officers can trigger automated verification emails to the issuing institution from within the platform, with HEC automatically copied on all correspondence. Responses are tracked in the system. Nothing happens outside the record. The Director General's signature, digitally issued at scale The equivalency certificate carries the Director General's official digital signature. In the previous process, this created a bottleneck — physical certificates waiting for signature, delays accumulating. HEC MIS structures this as the final step in a managed pipeline: by the time an application reaches the DG, it has been cleared by every review level. Signing triggers automatic certificate generation. There is no administrative work left to do. A national record of equivalency decisions Every application processed through HEC MIS — approved, rejected, or returned for more information — is part of a permanent, auditable record. Analytics on application volumes, processing times, high-risk country flags, and officer-level throughput are all available in the platform. This gives HEC leadership visibility into how the program is performing and where bottlenecks emerge. Irembo integration means no friction for applicants Because HEC MIS connects directly to Irembo — the platform Rwandans already use for government services — applicants submit through a familiar interface, pay through IremboPay, and receive status updates through the same portal. HEC MIS handles everything on the back end. The applicant never needs to know the internal system exists. Innovation Opportunities: HEC MIS has digitised and structured a previously manual national process. As the platform matures and the dataset of processed applications grows, a new set of capabilities becomes possible. 1. Processing Time Analytics and SLA Monitoring HEC MIS already captures timestamps at every stage of every application. The next step is turning that data into actionable performance intelligence — average time per review level, applications exceeding defined processing targets, officer throughput comparisons, and trend analysis over time. This would give HEC leadership the tools to manage service delivery against formal commitments, and identify where in the pipeline delays are consistently occurring. 2. AI-Assisted Document Review The volume of foreign qualification applications is likely to grow as Rwanda's economy attracts more international talent and more Rwandans return from studying abroad. AI-assisted tools could support L1 officers by flagging document inconsistencies, cross-referencing against known institutional formats, or surfacing applications with characteristics associated with high-risk submissions. The goal is not to replace officer judgement — it is to make that judgement faster and better-informed. 3. A National Qualifications Database Every approved equivalency creates a verified record linking a foreign qualification to its Rwandan equivalent. Over time, HEC MIS is accumulating what could become Rwanda's authoritative database of recognised foreign qualifications — by institution, country, and qualification type. This dataset has significant value beyond individual application processing. Employers verifying a candidate's credentials, institutions making admissions decisions, and policymakers tracking skills entering the country could all benefit from access to a structured, searchable qualifications registry. 4. Integration with Other Government Systems A foreign qualification that HEC has formally recognised should, ideally, flow automatically into other systems that need to know about it — the Rwanda Education Board, the professional regulatory bodies, the Rwanda National Identification Agency. Currently, the equivalency certificate is an endpoint. It could instead be a data point that triggers downstream recognition across government. This kind of system-to-system integration would reduce the burden on applicants who currently need to present their certificate separately to multiple institutions. 5. Applicant Self-Service Portal Today, applicants interact with HEC MIS only through Irembo — they see status updates but have limited visibility into what is happening with their application or what is expected of them at each stage. A lightweight applicant-facing layer within HEC MIS — showing the current review level, any outstanding information requests, and estimated processing timelines — would reduce inbound enquiries to HEC and give applicants a more dignified experience. 6. Regional Mutual Recognition Framework Rwanda is not the only country managing foreign qualification equivalency. EAC member states face the same challenge, and there are ongoing regional discussions about mutual recognition of qualifications. HEC MIS could become the infrastructure layer for Rwanda's participation in a regional qualifications framework — sharing verified equivalency data with partner countries and accepting reciprocal recognition data in return. This would position HEC as a regional leader in qualifications governance, and reduce processing times for qualifications from partner countries that are already well-understood. 21: GKK Fellowship Program Executive Summary The GKK Fellowship Program is a strategic initiative designed to create a curated network of skilled professionals that Global Kwik Koders can engage for project-based work, capacity building, and thought leadership. By leveraging our new Remera office space as a collaboration hub, we can build a sustainable talent ecosystem that strengthens our delivery capacity. This proposal outlines a comprehensive framework for attracting, engaging, and retaining top-tier professionals across software development, AI/ML, design, product management, and business development domains. The Fellowship model allows GKK to scale flexibly while maintaining quality standards and building long-term relationships with Rwanda's best talent. Strategic Objectives Build Scalable Delivery Capacity: Create a pre-vetted talent pool that can be rapidly deployed on government contracts (Ministry of Health, Ministry of Education) and commercial product development (Kwik Ride, Kwik Senda, Kwik Med AI, Kwik Pei). Reduce Hiring Risk & Costs: Fellowship engagement allows us to evaluate talent before making permanent commitments, significantly reducing hiring risk while avoiding traditional recruitment costs. Strengthen Proposal Competitiveness: Include Fellows' expertise and CVs in project proposals to demonstrate depth of capability to funders like GIZ, World Bank, and MasterCard Foundation. Create Community Value: Position GKK as a hub for professional growth in Rwanda's tech ecosystem, attracting talent through reputation and opportunity rather than just compensation. Support Series A Positioning: Demonstrate to investors a scalable talent model that can support rapid growth post-funding.
